blocks.text: Notes
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: 1. Successful completion of CS 700 with a grade of B or better is a prerequisite for CS 701.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: 2. A thorough literature review is likely to be part of most CS 701 research activities. However, the
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: CS 701 research activity should include a hands-on component (such as software development,
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: performing and analyzing experiments with existing techniques) beyond the literature review.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: Specify the hands-on activity within the “description of the research activity” field above.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: If necessary, you can attach an additional sheet to elaborate further on the description of
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: the research activity.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: 3. The CS 701 student will submit a professionally typed report to the CS faculty supervisor at
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: the end of the semester. In addition, all CS 701 students are required to give a short talk to
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: the public about their research at the end of the semester. Logistics of that meeting will be
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: announced by the CS department.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: 4. If there is a CS-affiliated faculty who will co-supervise the CS 701 project, their name should be
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: indicated next to the “CS faculty member name” field above, and they should co-sign the form.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: At the registrar level, the CS 701 registration will be made only under CS faculty names.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: 5. Submit the completed form to both csphd@gmu.edu and aydin@gmu.edu by e-mail (put
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: "[CS701 form]" in the subject line) by November 21, 2025.
